claims.text: The baseline alloy is a W-Ta-Cr-V refractory high-entropy alloy.
The baseline W-Ta-Cr-V alloy has a single-phase BCC structure.
The baseline alloy has high thermal stability.
The baseline W-Ta-Cr-V alloy has high irradiation stability, including resistance to dislocation-loop formation, small helium bubbles, and no radiation-induced grain-boundary segregation.
The baseline alloy has limited room-temperature ductility and moderate strength.
Hafnium should be added as a fifth principal element to W-Ta-Cr-V to form a quinary RHEA.
The appropriate Hf addition is expected to be on the order of a few atomic percent.
Adding Hf will modify local lattice distortion.
Hf may produce a fine nanoscale dispersion or a uniform strengthened solid solution without harmful precipitates.
Hf-enhanced lattice distortion will impede dislocation motion and increase solid-solution strengthening.
The high melting point and refractory-element compatibility of Hf will help preserve elevated-temperature microstructural stability.
Hf addition will suppress irradiation-induced defect formation, including dislocation loops and helium-bubble coalescence.
The Hf-modified alloy will have higher hardness and yield strength than baseline W-Ta-Cr-V.
The Hf-modified alloy will retain thermal stability and irradiation resistance similar to those of baseline W-Ta-Cr-V.
The hypothesis is intended to apply under high-temperature service conditions relevant to aerospace or nuclear applications.
The hypothesis is intended to apply under heavy-ion irradiation or helium implantation comparable to the baseline evaluations.
Excessive Hf may form unwanted intermetallic phases and cause embrittlement or microstructural coarsening.
Matched baseline and Hf-modified samples should be processed identically and compared after high-temperature annealing and ion irradiation.
Hardness, yield strength, phase stability, dislocation-loop density, and helium-bubble characteristics are measurable comparison outcomes.
Failure to improve mechanical performance significantly, or degradation of thermal or irradiation stability, would falsify the hypothesis.
